Industry "Pressure Loss Through Water Meters" table, printed identically by Rain Bird (reference sheet, rainbird.com/media/3573, 2007), Hunter (US catalog 2023, PDF page 196, "Typical Pressure Loss") and Toro/Irritrol (2026 catalog, PDF page 184). Not tied to a meter model: a generic displacement-meter curve. The table stops where the loss reaches 15.0 psi, at 20 gpm; that matches the commonly quoted AWWA C700 ceiling (15 psi at the safe maximum flow), but the C700 text itself is paywalled and was NOT checked, so this is not a transcription of the standard.

Badger Meter data sheet IDM-DS-00113-EN (June 2021; copy hosted by Instrumart): the table point is "Pressure Loss at Maximum Continuous Operation"; the curve points are digitised from the "Pressure Loss Charts" (log flow axis, 1 psi gridlines) at 600 dpi, +/-0.3 psi. Each curve passes within 0.4 psi of its own table point, which checks the reading. The October 2015 data sheet RDM-DS-00464 prints the same table values.

notes: Scope: manufacturer pressure-loss-vs-flow data for US residential irrigation devices. Each point is psi lost across the device at that flow. "read":"table" = a number printed in a table; "read":"curve" = digitised from a printed curve (method and tolerance in that device's note). Nothing is interpolated: a flow not listed has no value here; the caller decides whether to interpolate between listed points.

maxGpm: valves = the top of the maker's printed flow range; meters = the top of the typical operating range (the max-continuous figure is in the note); backflow = the approval-agency rated flow only where the sheet marks it on a labelled gridline, otherwise null and the marker position is described in the note. null = not printed.

Backflow loss charts (Watts, FEBCO, Zurn Wilkins, Apollo) are curves only; no maker prints a table. Their curves come from USC Foundation for Cross-Connection Control or independent-lab tests. Low-flow parts of overlapping multi-size charts were skipped wherever the curves could not be told apart.

Anti-siphon valves (Rain Bird ASVF, Hunter PGV-ASV, Toro EZ-Flo Plus anti-siphon) are listed as kind "valve" and their tables include the built-in atmospheric vacuum breaker. No loss chart was found for a standalone atmospheric vacuum breaker (AVB), so kind "avb" has no entries.

NOT FOUND / NOT USED: Rain Bird JTV (the only copy, a distributor mirror, could not be fetched and its column headers are reported ambiguous); Rain Bird 1-1/2" PGA and other 1-1/2"+ valves (left out as outside residential scope); Hunter's live site (blocks automated requests; its 2023 catalog was used instead); Watts 800M4 (non-QT) and 008PCQT; Conbraco/Apollo 4V-500 (the PVB4A successor is given instead); Neptune T-10 and Sensus SR II pressure-loss curves (product sheets 404 or blocked); the AWWA C700 standard text (paywalled).

Several hosts block scripted downloads (watts.com, zurn.com, hunterirrigation.com, plumbersstock.com). Watts/FEBCO sheets were taken from Watts' own devsc10.watts.com / watts.ca hosts with the same document ids as www.watts.com. Zurn and Apollo sheets come from distributor copies of the maker's PDF; the document number and revision are in each note so the original can be checked.

Rain Bird has published two different tables for DV and ASVF valves: the 2017 tech spec values (in the notes) are lower at low flow than the catalog values used for the points. The catalog (2017-2020 editions) is the later document.
